bull.b: The strong Q2 revenue increase shows improving adoption of PSQ’s continuing operations, while positive non-GAAP operating income indicates some emerging operating efficiency. If sustained, this combination could improve scalability and help narrow the company’s substantial reported losses.

A gross margin near 60% suggests PSQ’s core offerings retain meaningful economics before operating expenses. This provides a foundation for future operating leverage if revenue continues to scale and management can control costs, even though current overhead still produces substantial losses.

Exiting the non-core EveryLife brand could simplify PSQ’s portfolio, reduce distractions and concentrate management attention on payments and financial infrastructure. The planned cash proceeds may also strengthen resources available for the company’s continuing operations without requiring immediate equity issuance.

bear.b: The depth of PSQ’s operating and net losses indicates that revenue growth has not yet translated into sustainable operating leverage. Persistent losses can consume capital, constrain strategic investment and make the business more dependent on cost reductions or external financing over the coming quarters.

PSQ is still consuming cash rather than funding operations internally, and free cash flow deteriorated sharply versus the prior period. Continued cash burn reduces financial flexibility and increases the likelihood that additional capital or balance-sheet capacity will be needed to sustain growth.

Debt that is many times the reported equity base leaves PSQ with limited balance-sheet flexibility while losses continue. Elevated leverage can magnify financing pressure, restrict capital allocation choices and increase dilution or refinancing risk if cash consumption persists.
